extracted.intended_audience: users of Singular computer algebra system; mathematicians and computational algebra practitioners who write/maintain Singular code and libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Reference chapter describing Singular's built-in and user-defined data types, their syntax, semantics, operations, related functions, and examples. Intended as authoritative guidance for writing correct Singular code and libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: package (data type)
rubrics_metrics.description: The data type package is used to group identifiers into collections to avoid name collisions; important packages include Top (toplevel user identifiers and user-accessible library procedures) and Current (the current package name). Library-local identifiers go into a package derived from the library name with capitalization rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used mainly to avoid identifier collisions between libraries and user variables. See Section 3.8 on Libraries. Examples show creating packages and listing variables. Reserved package names: Top and Current.

rubrics_metrics.name: package declarations (syntax & purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: package name ; Purpose: defines a package (only relevant in special situations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage: package Test; then using Test::i, or package dummy = Test; kill Test; listvar(dummy); output examples demonstrate package scoping behavior. Declarations may be rare and used for special namespace control.

rubrics_metrics.name: package related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions for interacting with packages: exportto transfers an identifier to a specified package; importfrom generates a copy of an identifier from a specified package into the current package; listvar lists variables defined in a package; load/LIB loads a library or dynamic module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the referenced sections for full behavior. Use exportto/importfrom to move/copy identifiers across package boundaries; listvar helps inspect package contents; load/LIB loads libraries where package-local identifiers may be defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly (polynomial data type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Polynomials are basic data used by main algorithms in Singular, composed of finitely many terms (coefficient*monomial). Polynomials are always defined/accessed relative to a basering which determines coefficient type, indeterminate names, and monomial ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare a ring before defining polys. Example: ring r=32003,(x,y,z),dp; poly f=x3+y5+z2; Many polynomial operations and functions require an appropriate basering and monomial ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly declarations (syntax, purpose, default)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: poly name = poly expression ; Purpose: defines a polynomial. Default value: 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show literal polynomials, polynomials with exponentiation and indexed variables, and use of int variables in polynomial expressions. Demonstrates default printing and use of 'short' option to change output verbosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly expressions (what counts as polynomial expressions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A polynomial expression may be: (1) a monomial (no spaces allowed inside monomials), (2) a poly identifier, (3) a function returning poly, (4) polynomial expressions combined by +,-,*,/,^, (5) an int expression (type-converted), (6) a type cast to poly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monomials that contain indexed ring variables must be built using * and ^. Examples show valid vs invalid forms (e.g., 2*a(1) valid, but 2a(1) is a syntax error). Clarifies how 2*x^3 is parsed vs 2x^3.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly operations (operators and semantics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supported polynomial operations: + (addition), - (negation/subtraction), * (multiplication), / or div (division ignoring remainder for certain coeff fields), % or mod (remainder from division), ^ or ** (power by positive integer), comparators (<,<=,>,>=,==,<>) comparing leading monomials w.r.t ordering), and indexing to select monomials by position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division ignoring remainder implemented only over QQ, ZZ/p and certain field extensions. Examples illustrate arithmetic, division by monomials, comparators depending on ordering, and using intvec indexing to select monomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly related functions (list)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of functions related to polynomials: cleardenom, coef, coeffs, deg, diff, extgcd, factorize, finduni, gcd, homog, jacob, lead, leadcoef, leadexp, leadmonom, jet, ord, qhweight, reduce, rvar, simplify, size, subst, trace, var, varstr (and references to their sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed function has a specific behavior (e.g., cleardenom cancels denominators and divides by content; reduce computes normal form w.r.t. a standard base). See referenced sections for full signatures and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: proc (procedures data type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures are sequences of Singular commands in a special format used to extend the set of commands with user-defined commands; can be typed interactively or loaded from files (libraries). Files with procedure definitions following syntax rules are libraries loaded via LIB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures defined in libraries can include help strings and example sections; the example section executes on example proc_name;. Procedures defined interactively ignore help strings and cannot have an example section. Use static keyword for library-local (non-user-accessible) procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: proc declaration (syntax & semantics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: [static] proc proc_name [(<parameter list>) [<help string>] { <procedure body> } [example { <sequence of commands> } ]]. Purpose: defines a new function named proc_name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help string and example section are optional but mandatory for procedures listed in a library header. Example demonstrates defining milnor_number(proc) returning integer and printing messages; references to parameter list and help string sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: proc expression (lambda-like syntax)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: variable_name -> { expression(s) } Purpose: defines a new function within apply or for assigning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: apply(1..3,x->{x**2}); returns 1 4 9. See apply and proc sections for interactions with types and casting.

rubrics_metrics.name: procs with different argument types (branchTo behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism to branch to different procedures depending on runtime argument types: branchTo(string_expression, ... proc_name). The main procedure must be defined without an argument list and branchTo must be first statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows defining multiple p1,p21,p22 procedures and a dispatcher p() using branchTo to select implementation based on types (e.g., "int", "string"). ERROR can be used for unsupported types.

rubrics_metrics.name: resolution (intermediate representation type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Type 'resolution' is an intermediate representation retaining additional info from computing resolutions; enables use of partial results to compute Betti numbers or minimal resolutions. Resolutions must be defined w.r.t. a basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: to access elements of a resolution it must be assigned to a list — assignment completes computations and may take time. Direct bracket access causes implicit cast to list; examples show res, betti and listing components.

rubrics_metrics.name: resolution declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: resolution name = resolution expression ; Purpose: defines a resolution. Default: none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: resolution re=res(i,0); re; prints resolution; betti(re) returns Betti numbers. Converting to list reveals matrix generators and differentials; assignments may finish pending computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: resolution expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: A resolution expression may be (1) an identifier of type resolution, (2) a function returning a resolution, (3) a type cast to resolution from a list of ideals or modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Type conversion and casting. Use appropriate constructors (res, mres, etc.) to obtain resolution objects; details in syzygies/resolutions appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: resolution related functions (list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions: betti (Betti numbers), fres (free resolution of a standard basis), lres (free resolution), minres (minimize free resolution), mres (minimal free resolution and minimal generators), res (free resolution without changing ideal/module), sres (free resolution of a standard basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each function has distinct behavior w.r.t. standard bases and minimality. See referenced sections for usage and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: ring (basering concept & requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rings describe properties of polynomials, ideals, etc.; almost all computations in Singular require a basering. Rings determine coefficient types, variable names, and monomial ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rings and orderings for detailed discussion. Many data types and commands require an appropriate basering to be current.

rubrics_metrics.name: ring declarations (syntax, purpose, defaults)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: ring name = (coefficients), (names of ring variables), (ordering); or ring name = cring [ names of ring variables ]. Default: (ZZ/32003)[x,y,z]. Purpose: declares a ring and sets it as the actual basering; second form sets ordering to (dp,C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coefficients can be cring (QQ, ZZ, ZZ/m), integers, real, complex, integer lists, etc. Names must be a list of (possibly indexed) names. Ordering is a list of block orderings (lp, dp, Dp, rp, ls, ds, Ds, rs, wp, ws, M(...), c, C) and may include weights or matrices. See examples and ordering references. Parentheses optional when single entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: ring related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions related to rings: charstr, keepring, npars, nvars, ordstr, parstr, qring, ringlist, setring, varstr and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions describe characteristics (charstr), move between ring levels (keepring), report numbers of parameters/variables, monomial ordering strings, names of parameters/variables, and construct quotient rings (qring). Each has a dedicated section with examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: ring operations (construct & compare)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations: + constructs a new ring k[X,Y] from k1[X] and k2[Y] (variable sets must be distinct). == and <> compare two rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines: neither ground fields may be R or C; if characteristics differ one must be Q; at most one may have parameters; algebraic extensions of Z/p must not be defined by charstr of type (p^n,a). Example demonstrates combining rings and interpreting resulting coefficient and ordering blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: qring declaration (quotient ring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: qring name = ideal expression ; Purpose: declares a quotient ring (basering modulo ideal expression) and sets it as current basering. Default: none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations based on standard bases operate with residue classes; other operations use polynomial objects. Examples show std(i) to form ideal, reduce to compute simplification, and comparisons between polynomials vs residue classes using reduce.

rubrics_metrics.name: string (string data type & usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strings are used for output and creating commands at runtime; many types convert to string. String constants are characters between quotes (including newline). Strings support concatenation (+) and form semigroup; empty string is "". Comma between strings forms an expression list printed with separating blank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: String can be used to format output or build runtime commands (execute). Examples show concatenation and mixing strings with numeric conversions via string(...). Note the difference between + (concatenate) and comma (print-list).

rubrics_metrics.name: string declarations (syntax & default)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: string name = string expression ; or string name = list of string expressions ; Purpose: defines a string variable. Default: "" (empty string).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show escaping quotes and concatenating strings. Using comma versus + yields different printed output (comma inserts a space).

rubrics_metrics.name: string expressions (what qualifies)
rubrics_metrics.description: A string expression is: (1) a sequence of characters between unescaped quotes, (2) an identifier of type string, (3) a function returning string, (4) a substring via bracket operator, (5) a type cast to string, (6) string expressions combined by +.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: substring operations s[2,4] returns substring of length 4 starting at pos 2 (padded with blanks if necessary); s[position] returns single character; s[position..position] returns substring range. See type conversion section for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: string type cast (string(...))
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: string(expression [, expression2, ...]) Purpose: converts each expression to a string and concatenates them. Elements of intvec, intmat, ideal, module, matrix, and list are separated by commas; no newlines inserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applied to a list, elements of intvec, intmat, ideal, module, matrix, and list become indistinguishable (flattening). Examples show string(intvec(1,2,3)) -> "1,2,3" and string(r) for a ring prints its representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: string operations (operators & semantics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators: + for concatenation; <=, >=, ==, <> for lexicographic comparison by ASCII; bracket indexing for characters and substrings; bracket with intvec returns expression list of characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexes start at 1. Examples illustrate extracting characters, substrings, concatenating with other strings and formatting with >> << markers. Assignment to substrings permitted (s[2] = "BC").

rubrics_metrics.name: string related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions: charstr, execute, find, names, nameof, option, ordstr, parstr, read, size, sprintf, typeof, varstr and others related to string handling and interaction with interpreter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: execute runs a string as a command; find locates substring positions; read reads files; sprintf formats strings. See respective sections for signatures and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: vector (free module element data type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vectors are elements of a free module over the basering with basis gen(1), gen(2), ... Each vector belongs to a free module of rank equal to the largest generator index with non-zero coefficient; zero-coefficient generators may be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vectors must be surrounded by square brackets. Vectors can be treated as elements of higher-rank modules by adding trailing zeros or generators. Example shows mixed polynomial entries and use of gen(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: vector declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: vector name = vector expression ; Purpose: defines a vector of polynomials (element of a free module). Default: [0].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates building a vector using polynomials and gen(5) to indicate rank-5 free module. Vectors printed as lists of entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: vector expressions (allowed forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: A vector expression may be: (1) a vector identifier, (2) a function returning vector, (3) a polynomial expression embedded as p -> p*gen(1), (4) vector expressions combined by + or -, (5) polynomial and vector expression combined by *, (6) a type cast to vector using brackets [ , ].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show ordering affecting printed priority by components; multiplication by polynomial scales entries. Use type conversion when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: vector operations (operators & semantics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations: + addition, - negation/subtraction, / division by a monomial (non-divisible terms yield 0), comparators (<,<=,>,>=,==,<>) considering leading terms, bracket indexing to access entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show subtraction and indexing returning entries. Division by monomial only keeps divisible terms; careful with monomial orderings affecting comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: vector related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions: cleardenom (quotient by content), coeffs, deg, diff, gen, homog, jet, lead, leadcoef, leadexp, leadmonom, nrows, ord, reduce, simplify, size, subst and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many vector-related operations mirror polynomial ones (leading term, degree, simplification). See referenced sections for concrete usage and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: user defined types (newstruct definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: User defined types are non-empty lists with fixed size whose elements are accessed by names (not indices); element types are predefined and may depend on a ring. Elements with ring-dependence can only be accessed if their base ring is the current basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a new type via newstruct(name, string_expression) or newstruct(name, existing_type, string_expression) where the last string lists member types and names. Member names restricted to alphanumeric starting with a letter; duplicate names last one wins.

rubrics_metrics.name: declaration of objects of a user defined type
rubrics_metrics.description: After newstruct, declare objects by type name (e.g., nt A;). As long as ring-dependent members are unset, no ring is required to exist for the object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment of ring-dependent members later requires an appropriate basering. Copying objects (nt B = A) works as usual; uninitialized members show ?? or defaults when printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: access to elements of a user defined type
rubrics_metrics.description: Access elements via dot operator: <object>.<element name>. Ring-dependent elements additionally have r_<element name> entry for the corresponding ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A.b=poly(1) requires ring to be set; A.r_b shows the ring-dependent representation. Elements are printed by name; type checking enforced on assignments to elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: commands for user defined types (installing kernel commands)
rubrics_metrics.description: User types can be integrated with kernel commands by providing procedures and installing them via system("install", user_type, kernel_command, p, number_of_args). The user_type and command must be strings. Some kernel commands accept variable arg counts (use 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual lists kernel commands and required number of args (binary operands, unary functions, functions with 2 or 3 args, and variable-arg functions). Example shows installing pretty-print and custom + operator for type nt.

rubrics_metrics.name: assignments for user defined types (custom constructors)
rubrics_metrics.description: By default assignment requires same user type (no automatic conversion). The = operator can be overridden to write custom constructors via system("install", user_type, "=", p, 1). This custom constructor handles conversions for assignments of other types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows wrapping polys into a 'wrapping' type with system install of '='; then assignments like wrapping w = x+1 or w = int(1) work due to conversions. Custom constructor also enables generic type conversion idiom described in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: cone (convex rational polyhedral cone type and requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular integrates gfanlib to support convex objects; 'cone' is a type representing convex rational polyhedral cones generated by finitely many half-lines or as solution sets of homogeneous rational linear inequalities/equations. Cones have lineality space and rays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LIB"gfan.lib" to load gfanlib. Some operations require polymake. Two main ways to define cones in Singular: coneViaPoints and coneViaInequalities. Examples show declaring cone c and cone c = 17 (ambient dim convenience). See gfanlib section for installation and interface details.

rubrics_metrics.name: fan (polyhedral fan type and constructors)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fan is a collection of cones closed under intersections and faces. Constructible via various convenience constructors: fan f; fan f = emptyFan(int n); fan f = fullFan(int n); optional symmetry group intmat G may be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructors document ambient dimension, presence of cones, lineality space and optional symmetry subgroup generated by rows of G. Singular will validate permutation rows in G. See gfanlib section and examples for usage.
